solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: College to offer additional weapon

parts.note: to lay is to offer or put forward, as in laying odds or laying a proposal before someone
more means additional or extra

explanation.surface: A college proposes acquiring yet another weapon for its collection.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLAYMORE is a large Scottish two-handed sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland broadsword is a historic example of a bladed arm used in battle.

clue.text: Vessel for a service in church

indicators.note: in places the service words inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A container used during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests worship, but means an armed service, the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass vessel for serving wine or water.

clue.text: Married man who later rued arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband who regrets his choice afterward.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer is a married person who is unfaithful to the spouse.

clue.text: Intends to make money

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has something in mind has it as their purpose; resources or wealth are one's financial wherewithal.

clue.text: Unexpected deterioration makes Romeo slip away

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
time is said to elapse when it slips away

explanation.surface: A sudden decline causes a lover to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a return to illness after apparent recovery, a sudden decline.

clue.text: Outlaw in favour of offer

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for a motion
a bid is an offer, as at auction

explanation.surface: Someone supports making an offer for a wanted criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit, but here it is the verb: to ban.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to prohibit it, the verb sense of banning.

clue.text: Lose sense of proportion when soldiers tuck into ham

indicators.note: tuck into means put inside, so the soldiers go into the word for ham

parts.note: to ham is to overact on stage
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Things get out of hand when troops start eating the ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' and 'ham' suggest eating, but ham is the verb for bad acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond more strongly than warranted, failing to keep perspective.

clue.text: Beef is excellent

explanation.definitionFit: Corned meat in tins is called bully beef, and an old exclamation of approval uses the word to mean splendid.

clue.text: Reveal record on waste

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to lose is to waste, as in losing time

explanation.surface: Someone exposes a record of squandering.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts DISC above LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose something is to make it known, which is to reveal it.

clue.text: Wild USA rebel can be employed again

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the following words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An unruly American rebel might still find another job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be used a second time is fit to be employed again.

clue.text: FT staff promote retiring film director

parts.note: the staff of the Financial Times, writing in the newspaper, would refer to themselves as we

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so the word for promote goes backwards

parts.note: to sell something is to promote or push it

explanation.surface: Newspaper employees publicise a film director who is stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'FT staff' is the newspaper speaking of itself as 'we'; 'retiring' turns only the promote word backwards. Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles was the celebrated American director of Citizen Kane, so he exemplifies a filmmaker.

clue.text: Many poke fun at Yank

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, so it stands for many
to rag someone is to tease or poke fun at them

explanation.surface: Lots of people mock an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag is to pull forcibly, which is what a yank does.

clue.text: Goddesses succeeded after fellow had a meal

indicators.note: after places the letter for succeeded behind the other pieces

parts.note: ate means had a meal
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Some goddesses prospered once a man had eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fates are the three goddesses of Greek myth who spin, measure and cut the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The three mythic sisters controlling human destiny were divine beings, a classical example of goddesses.

clue.text: Picture requires light through doorway

indicators.note: through puts the ray of light passing inside the doorway word

parts.note: a portal is a doorway or gateway
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A painting needs sunlight streaming in through an open door.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction or representation, which is what a picture provides.

clue.text: Charlie leaves boat for shrine

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter for Charlie is dropped from the boat word

parts.note: a coracle is a small round wicker boat used in Wales
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie abandons his boat and heads to a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a person leaving, but is just the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece an oracle was the holy place where a god was consulted, such as Delphi, hence a shrine.

clue.text: Fighting under officer, more than one die showing timidity

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the fighting word below the officer

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
war is fighting
dice is the plural of die

explanation.surface: Gambling under a commander in wartime reveals a lack of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is lack of courage, the condition of being timid or fearful.

clue.text: Help in making out with good girls

parts.note: lasses is a British and Scottish word for girls

explanation.surface: Seems to describe assistance with romantic fumbling with nice young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making out' suggests romance, but here it means seeing clearly, so spectacles help.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are an aid to vision, helping the wearer make out things they could not otherwise see.

clue.text: Pitch where drinks are taken through a straw

indicators.note: taken through puts the drinks inside the word for straw

parts.note: a straw is a dried stalk of grain
ales are drinks of beer

explanation.surface: A place where beer is sipped through a drinking straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a sports field, but means a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch is a persuasive spiel delivered to sell something, i.e. sales talk.

clue.text: Municipality supports change of rota leading to outrage

indicators.note: supports in a down clue puts the municipality below the other piece
change of means the letters of the rota are altered in order

parts.note: a city is a municipality

explanation.surface: A town council backs a rota shake-up that provokes outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' turns ROTA into ATRO.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a shocking act of cruelty, an outrage.

clue.text: Brawl interrupts fine play in football match

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the brawl word goes inside the word for fine

parts.note: thin means fine, as in fine thread
a row is a noisy quarrel or brawl

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out mid-game and a fine is imposed during the football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty, but it means slender.
explanation.definitionFit: When the ball leaves the field at the side, play restarts by hurling it back with both hands, a move in soccer.

clue.text: A number working for a time

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
on means working or functioning, as with a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A digit operates for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is one particular time of the day.

clue.text: Unsettle the conductor

definitions.meaning: to make someone nervous or flustered
Sir Simon ..., the British orchestra conductor

explanation.definitionFit: To rattle is to unnerve someone; Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor of the Berlin Philharmonic and LSO.

clue.text: Deer eat head of lettuce in the US

indicators.note: eat means take in, so the deer word swallows the head word

parts.note: a roe is a small European deer
main means chief or head, as in head office

explanation.surface: Deer munch the top of a lettuce in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of lettuce' looks like one phrase, but 'head' gives MAIN and 'of lettuce' leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Romaine is the American name for cos lettuce.

clue.text: Be inclined to keep work of the highest quality

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the work word goes within the inclined word

parts.note: to tend is to be inclined to do something
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Being disposed to retain only premium work.
explanation.definitionFit: The top end of a market is its upper tier, the most expensive and finest goods.

clue.text: Requisition brotherhood's criminal record

parts.note: an order is a brotherhood, such as a religious or chivalric order
form is British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: A fraternity's history of offences is under investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a person with previous convictions 'has form'.
explanation.definitionFit: A requisition is a formal written request for goods, made on a document listing items wanted.

clue.text: Dutch king's private sink

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
own means private or personal, as in one's own room

explanation.surface: A Dutch monarch's personal washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' is the verb: to go under.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown is to sink under water and perish, or to submerge something.

clue.text: Club in which the password is courage

indicators.note: in which says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A secret club where you get in by saying 'courage'.
explanation.walkthrough: The Password Is Courage is a 1962 British war film.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a nightclub where people dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Shot a scene

parts.note: a dram is a small shot of spirits

explanation.surface: Filming a sequence on set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like filming, but means a measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a scene is making a drama, a fuss or emotional display.

clue.text: It's paradoxical that one club backs another

indicators.note: backs means stands behind, so one and club follow the other club

parts.note: another club, here a golf iron
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for club, as in card suits

explanation.surface: A golfer finds it odd that one club props up another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' sets the theme, so 'another' is a second club: a golf IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something paradoxical is contrary to expectation in a wry way, the essence of irony.

clue.text: Give a car overhaul in official residence

indicators.note: an overhaul takes something apart and rebuilds it, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to service a vehicle at a government residence.
explanation.walkthrough: A vicarage is the house provided for a Church of England vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar's house belongs to the parish and goes with the post, an official residence for the clergyman.

clue.text: Rodney knocked about over there

indicators.note: knocked about means battered, so the name's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Poor Rodney gets beaten up in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word for a place at a distance, out over there.

clue.text: Commented about evangelist to journalist

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Mark is one of the four evangelists, the Gospel writers
ED is short for editor, a crossword stand-in for a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone spoke to a reporter about a preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to make a comment, so having remarked is having commented.
